note: The output-coverage census (`script/m14/tmp/elixir-declaration-census.ts` — per DECLARATION FORM, does a symbol or edge get published?) found the last real gap: `@callback` / `@macrocallback` emitted a file-level `Behaviours` pattern flag and NOTHING else. Measured 165 sites in a 100-file sample of elixir+phoenix+ash and 98 in a 171-file ecto_sql+ecto+wallaby sample, 0 covered. A module may declare a behaviour surface with no `def` at all (`Callback.Probe` below), so the callback existed NOWHERE in the index. Three sub-decisions, each pinned here: (1) a callback is a DECLARATION — `isDeclaration: true` at the top level (the field the indexer binds to brain_symbol.is_declaration, #612, and the one the C and Clean lanes set for their prototypes), because a `def …, do: body` sibling makes the merged symbol a DEFINITION and the flag is then removed; (2) a bodiless `def` head is a declaration for the same reason, detected structurally (no `do_block` and no `do:` pair inside the def's `arguments` — the pair is NESTED there, not a sibling, which is what the first version of this check got wrong and how every `def f(x), do: y` briefly read as a head); (3) identity is shared with the function merge key, so `@callback load(t)` + `def load(x)` is ONE `load` symbol carrying the spec, not two symbols for one function. `@optional_callbacks` annotates instead of declaring: the names ride the protocol/module metadata and stamp the matching members. Extent follows EX-D16 (first..last of everything the symbol is: the spec is part of the surface, `clauseRanges` is not, because a callback is not a clause). The NEGATIVE half is pinned through forbidSymbols, because matchConstraints compares by value and an expectation cannot say "this field is absent" — a symbol that wrongly carried isDeclaration (or a head wrongly counted as a second clause) would match the forbid entry and fail the fixture. EX-A16 (the store seam, found by `script/m14/tmp/elixir-store-roundtrip.ts` — a real index through the REAL parallel indexer, read back in SQL): the declaration fact has to ride BOTH the top-level field and `metadata.isDeclaration`, because that is the single key the pool worker carries to the store phase (pool-worker.ts, the #612 seam comment) and the C analyzer publishes it that way. With only the top-level field the worker's symbol reconstruction dropped it and `brain_symbol.is_declaration` came out NULL for every elixir declaration — 0 rows on a real index, invisible to every fixture, because fixtures never pass through the worker. The `meta.isDeclaration` pins below are the analyzer half; the SQL round-trip is the seam half.
